name: Mebolazine (Dymethazine)
summary: A withdrawn oral steroid, a dimer of methasterone, that resurfaced in gray-market supplements; no human studies exist.
lead: Mebolazine, also called dimethazine or dymethazine, is a synthetic, orally active anabolic-androgenic steroid. It is a 17α-alkylated derivative of dihydrotestosterone and an unusual dimer of methasterone, two units joined by an azine group.

name: Mestanolone
summary: An old oral 17-methyl DHT steroid: strongly androgenic, weakly anabolic, mostly discontinued; no modern trials.
lead: Mestanolone (methylandrostanolone, 17α-methyldihydrotestosterone) is a synthetic androgen and anabolic steroid, a 17α-methylated derivative of dihydrotestosterone (DHT). The methyl group makes it active by mouth, unlike DHT itself.

name: Stenbolone
summary: A DHT-derived anabolic steroid whose acetate ester was an old injectable; known today mostly from metabolism studies.
lead: Stenbolone (2-methyl-Δ1-dihydrotestosterone) is a synthetic androgen and anabolic steroid derived from dihydrotestosterone, related to drostanolone and 1-testosterone. Wikipedia states the compound itself was never marketed.

name: Mepitiostane (Thioderon)
summary: Japanese oral prodrug of the antiestrogen steroid epitiostanol, sold as a breast-cancer and renal-anemia drug; no appearance studies exist.
lead: Mepitiostane (brand name Thioderon) is an orally active synthetic steroid of the dihydrotestosterone group that acts as an antiestrogen and a weak anabolic-androgenic steroid. It is a prodrug, meaning it is converted in the body to epitiostanol, the active compound.

name: Epitiostanol
summary: Injectable Japanese antiestrogen steroid (Thiodrol) used for breast cancer; the muscle-building angle has no human data behind it.
lead: Epitiostanol (brand name Thiodrol) is a synthetic steroid of the dihydrotestosterone group that acts as an antiestrogen and as a comparatively weak anabolic-androgenic steroid. It has been used in Japan as an antineoplastic drug for breast cancer since 1977.

name: Furazabol
summary: Oral Japanese anabolic steroid, close cousin of stanozolol, best known in the West from the Ben Johnson doping inquiry; no modern human trials.
lead: Furazabol is a synthetic, orally active anabolic-androgenic steroid that has been marketed in Japan since 1969. It is a 17α-alkylated derivative of dihydrotestosterone and is structurally close to stanozolol, differing in having a furazan ring where stanozolol has a pyrazole ring.

name: Oxabolone cipionate
summary: Obscure injectable 19-nor steroid ester once marketed in Europe as Steranabol; almost nothing is published about it.
lead: Oxabolone cipionate (also spelled cypionate) is a synthetic injected anabolic-androgenic steroid of the 19-nortestosterone (nandrolone) group. It is the C17β cypionate ester and a prodrug of oxabolone, and it carried the developmental code FI-5852. It has been marketed in Europe under the brand names Steranabol Depo and Steranabol Ritardo.

name: Ethylestrenol (Maxibolin)
summary: Old oral 19-nor anabolic steroid, now veterinary-only; Wikipedia calls it a very weak muscle-builder and there are no appearance trials.
lead: Ethylestrenol (also ethyloestrenol; brand names Maxibolin and Orabolin) is a synthetic oral androgen and anabolic steroid with progestogenic activity, derived from nandrolone by 17α-alkylation. It was first described in 1959, approved for medical use in 1961, and approved in the United States in 1964.

name: Norethandrolone (Nilevar)
summary: One of the first oral anabolic steroids (1950s); documented cholestasis and liver injury ended most use, and only a 1959 weight-gain study speaks to muscle.
lead: Norethandrolone (brand names Nilevar and Pronabol) is a synthetic, orally taken androgen and anabolic steroid of the 19-nortestosterone group, a 17α-ethyl derivative of nandrolone. G. D. Searle synthesized it in 1953, initially as a progestin, and introduced it medically as an anabolic steroid in 1956. Wikipedia describes it as the first anabolic steroid marketed with a favorable separation of anabolic and androgenic effects.

name: Mibolerone (Cheque Drops)
summary: A veterinary oral steroid for dogs that circulates in bodybuilding circles as a hyper-potent pre-workout; no human trials exist.
lead: Mibolerone, also called dimethylnortestosterone (DMNT) and sold under the brand names Cheque Drops and Matenon, is a synthetic, orally active anabolic-androgenic steroid derived from nandrolone. It was marketed by the Upjohn Company as a veterinary drug whose labeled purpose was to suppress estrus (heat) in adult female dogs . It is not approved for human use.
claims: Cheque Drops are the strongest oral steroid for strength and aggression.
Its short action makes it useful as a pre-workout "on demand" compound.
It can be used without the downsides of other oral steroids.

name: Bolasterone (Finaject)
summary: An obscure Upjohn-era veterinary oral steroid, now mostly a name in anti-doping detection papers.
lead: Bolasterone, chemically 7-alpha,17-alpha-dimethyltestosterone, is a synthetic, orally active anabolic-androgenic steroid developed by the Upjohn Company for veterinary use. Its 17-alpha-methyl group improves oral bioavailability and its 7-alpha-methyl group is shared with its isomer calusterone .

name: Chlorodehydromethyltestosterone (Turinabol / Oral Turinabol)
summary: The oral steroid of East German doping fame; well documented in history and detection science, untested as a treatment.
lead: Chlorodehydromethyltestosterone (CDMT, DHCMT), sold as Oral-Turinabol and nicknamed Tbol, is an oral anabolic-androgenic steroid, the 4-chloro derivative of metandienone. It was the first original product of the East German pharmaceutical company Jenapharm, patented in 1961, introduced clinically in 1965 and discontinued in 1994 .

name: Clostebol (4-chlorotestosterone)
summary: A chlorinated testosterone mostly known from skin creams and doping cases, with no appearance trials.
lead: Clostebol, also called 4-chlorotestosterone, is a synthetic anabolic-androgenic steroid derived from testosterone by adding a chlorine atom at the 4-position. It is usually formulated as an ester such as clostebol acetate, caproate or propionate .

name: Danazol
summary: A prescription antigonadotropin steroid for endometriosis and angioedema; no evidence for appearance use.
lead: Danazol is an oral synthetic steroid derived from ethisterone. It has weak androgenic and anabolic activity, along with antigonadotropic, progestogenic and functional antioestrogenic effects. It is a prescription drug used mainly for endometriosis, with approved or off-label use in hereditary angioedema, fibrocystic breast disease and some blood disorders .

name: Tibolone (Livial)
summary: A menopause drug with weak androgenic activity; heavily trialled for menopause, never for looks.
lead: Tibolone, sold as Livial and under other brand names, is an oral synthetic steroid with weak estrogenic, progestogenic and androgenic activity, classed as a selective tissue estrogenic activity regulator (STEAR). It is prescribed to postmenopausal women for hot flushes, vaginal atrophy and prevention of osteoporosis .

name: Gestrinone
summary: A weakly androgenic endometriosis steroid and the parent of the THG designer steroid; nothing studied for looks.
lead: Gestrinone is a synthetic steroid medication derived from 19-nortestosterone that combines progestogenic, antiprogestogenic, antiestrogenic and weak androgenic activity. It was introduced for medical use in 1986 and is marketed mainly for endometriosis, under brand names such as Dimetrose and Nemestran, in a limited number of countries; it is not available in the United States.

name: Testolactone (Teslac)
summary: A discontinued first-generation steroidal aromatase inhibitor once used for breast cancer; nothing tested for looks.
lead: Testolactone, sold as Teslac, is a steroidal first-generation aromatase inhibitor that was used as an anticancer drug for advanced breast cancer in postmenopausal women. It was first approved in the United States in 1970 and was discontinued in 2008.

name: Formestane (Lentaron)
summary: An injectable steroidal aromatase inhibitor for breast cancer, now withdrawn; nothing tested for looks.
lead: Formestane, sold as Lentaron, is a steroidal aromatase inhibitor that was given as an intramuscular depot injection to treat estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer in postmenopausal women. It is not orally active, was not approved by the US FDA, and the injectable form used in Europe has been withdrawn.

name: Fadrozole
summary: A nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitor used for breast cancer in Japan and as a lab tool; nothing tested for looks.
lead: Fadrozole (brand name Afema, Novartis) is a selective, nonsteroidal, oral aromatase inhibitor that is or has been used in Japan for breast cancer. It is classed as a Type II (reversible) inhibitor that binds the heme group of the aromatase enzyme.

name: Vorozole
summary: A discontinued third-generation aromatase inhibitor now used as a brain-imaging tracer; nothing tested for looks.
lead: Vorozole (developmental code R-76713, tentative brand name Rizivor) is a triazole-based, third-generation nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitor that was investigated as an anticancer drug. Clinical development stopped after a comparison with megestrol acetate showed no difference in median survival, and anastrozole, letrozole and exemestane became the standard agents.

name: Aminoglutethimide (Cytadren)
summary: An old adrenal-steroid and aromatase blocker with a rough side-effect profile; cortisol-cutting for physique is untested.
lead: Aminoglutethimide is an oral nonsteroidal glutarimide, sold under names including Cytadren, Elipten and Orimeten. It was introduced in 1960 as an anticonvulsant, then found to inhibit steroid synthesis, and was later used for Cushing's syndrome, postmenopausal breast cancer and prostate cancer. It was among the first adrenal steroidogenesis inhibitors and the first aromatase inhibitor used clinically.

name: ATD (1,4,6-androstatrienedione)
summary: A prohormone-era supplement aromatase inhibitor with lab data behind its mechanism and no human trials behind any look-related claim.
lead: ATD (1,4,6-androstatriene-3,17-dione) is a steroid-type compound described as an irreversible aromatase inhibitor, meaning it binds the enzyme that converts androgens into estrogens and permanently inactivates it . It was sold in over-the-counter bodybuilding and prohormone-era supplements, reportedly until around 2009, and is discussed in muscle-building circles as a way to limit estrogen conversion .

name: 6-OXO (4-androstene-3,6,17-trione)
summary: A prohormone-era aromatase inhibitor with an uncontrolled study showing hormone shifts and no body-composition change, and regulatory warnings.
lead: 6-OXO (4-androstene-3,6,17-trione, also 4-AT) is an oral supplement ingredient described as a potent, irreversible aromatase inhibitor that may raise the testosterone-to-estrogen ratio . It has been used mainly by people using steroids or prohormones, who say it limits estrogen rise and gynecomastia risk, and after cycles to shorten recovery of testicular function .

name: Damiana extract (Turnera diffusa)
summary: A traditional aphrodisiac herb with a lab report of anti-aromatase constituents and no human trials of the extract on its own.
lead: Damiana (Turnera diffusa) is a small shrub native to southern Texas, Mexico, Central and South America and the Caribbean. It has been used in Mexican liqueurs, herbal teas and smoking blends, and in 19th-century patent medicines promoted as an aphrodisiac .

name: White button mushroom extract
summary: A common food whose extracts inhibit aromatase in lab assays; human work is cancer-focused and not about looks.
lead: White button mushroom (Agaricus bisporus) is the common cultivated mushroom, grown in more than 70 countries; its brown form is sold as cremini and the mature form as portobello . Extracts of it are discussed as a food-derived aromatase inhibitor, meaning a substance that might reduce conversion of androgens to estrogens .

name: Afimoxifene (4-hydroxytamoxifen)
summary: The active form of tamoxifen, studied as a breast gel in women; use for male gynecomastia has no published trials.
lead: Afimoxifene, also called 4-hydroxytamoxifen (4-OHT), is an active metabolite of tamoxifen and a selective estrogen receptor modulator (SERM). It is an investigational drug, developed under the tentative brand name TamoGel as a topical gel for breast conditions .

name: Raloxifene (Evista)
summary: A prescription SERM approved for women's bone and breast risk, used off-label by men for gynecomastia on thin evidence.
lead: Raloxifene (brand name Evista) is a selective estrogen receptor modulator (SERM) approved in the US for treating and preventing osteoporosis in postmenopausal women and for reducing the risk of invasive breast cancer in postmenopausal women with osteoporosis or at high risk . It acts as an estrogen agonist in bone and an antagonist in breast and uterine tissue .
claims: Gyno may come back after stopping
Surgery is preferable to the drug

name: Toremifene
summary: A tamoxifen-like SERM approved for breast cancer and used off-label for gynecomastia; evidence for appearance use is thin and the label carries a QT warning.
lead: Toremifene, sold mainly under the brand name Fareston, is a selective estrogen receptor modulator (SERM) and a chlorinated analogue of tamoxifen. In the United States its only approved use is the treatment of metastatic breast cancer in postmenopausal women whose tumors are estrogen-receptor positive or of unknown status, and it is taken as a 60 mg oral tablet .

name: Fulvestrant (Faslodex)
summary: An injectable pure antiestrogen (SERD) used for breast cancer; no studies for appearance use.
lead: Fulvestrant, sold as Faslodex and as generics, is an antiestrogen given by intramuscular injection. It is the first selective estrogen receptor degrader (SERD) approved for medical use and is used for hormone receptor-positive breast cancer in postmenopausal women .

name: Bazedoxifene
summary: A menopause and osteoporosis SERM; nothing in the literature ties it to looks.
lead: Bazedoxifene is a third-generation selective estrogen receptor modulator (SERM) of the 2-phenylindole class, taken by mouth. It is used for the prevention of postmenopausal osteoporosis and, combined with conjugated estrogens as Duavee or Duavive, for menopausal vasomotor symptoms .
